chapter: Russell's band, records and Armstrong in the studio
title: Metcalf's ideas and the young band's good time
summary: Metcalf was the lively one and the young band enjoyed itself as much as the public did.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I remember you used to say that Metcalf was full of ideas.

Oh yeah, he was full of ideas. Everybody had some kind of ideas. Some wasn't so good and some wasn't...one of them things. But who knows what's good or bad? But Metcalf, he was the lively one in the band. You know, he always had ideas and he was always playing this, that and the other, and jokin' and carryin' on.

It was always something going on in the band. It was a young band. Everybody was young in the band, and they behaved just like young people should. You know what I mean? We wasn't just sittin' up on the stand lookin' dead. There was something goin' on... We were the happiest people in the place!
Well, did you have any sense that you were creating music that was important to you and maybe to others?
It was important to everybody that heard it! Ha-ha. People were out there to have a good time, and
we were there to have a good time! And naturally, your music brings it out. Yeah, the band had as good a time as the public did.
